subject: math
title: Quadrilaterals and Congruence: Properties, Diagonals, Symmetry and Congruent Shapes
seo_title: Grade 6 Quadrilaterals and Congruent Shapes Worksheets: Diagonals and Symmetry (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Create and analyse designs that include translated, rotated, and reflected two-dimensional shapes; list the geometric properties of quadrilaterals, including diagonals, rotational symmetry, and line symmetry, and identify and construct congruent shapes
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on quadrilaterals for the Ontario curriculum: name squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids and kites from their properties, diagonals, line and rotational symmetry, and congruent shapes on dot paper. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: Name a quadrilateral by what it must have: a square is also a rectangle and a rhombus.
key_sub: Check the diagonals (equal? cut in half? at right angles?), the lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry. Congruent shapes match exactly after a slide, turn or flip.
body_html:
Name a quadrilateral by its properties

A quadrilateral has 4 straight sides. Its name comes from what it must have: equal sides, right angles and parallel sides. Tick marks show equal sides, small squares show right angles and arrows show parallel sides.

ShapeWhat it must have
Rectangle4 right angles
Rhombus4 equal sides
Square4 right angles and 4 equal sides (so it is a rectangle and a rhombus)
Parallelogram2 pairs of parallel sides (opposite sides and opposite angles are equal)
Trapezoidexactly 1 pair of parallel sides
Kite2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other

Some books say a trapezoid has at least one pair of parallel sides. Every trapezoid in this unit has exactly one pair, so both meanings agree. Every kite in this unit is a kite that is not a rhombus.

Example 1

A quadrilateral has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm in order, and no parallel sides. What is it?

The equal sides are next to each other, not opposite. Two pairs of equal sides next to each other make a kite.

Answer: a kite

Diagonals

A diagonal joins two corners that are not next to each other. Every quadrilateral has 2 diagonals. Ask three questions: Are they equal? Do they cut each other in half? Do they cross at right angles?

ShapeLines of symmetryRotational symmetryDiagonals equal?Cut each other in half?Cross at right angles?
Square4order 4YesYesYes
Rectangle2order 2YesYesNo
Rhombus2order 2NoYesYes
Parallelogram0order 2NoYesNo
Kite1order 1NoOnly one is cut in halfYes
Trapezoid with equal slanted sides1order 1YesNoNo

The table shows shapes that are not special cases. For example, a rhombus that is also a square has equal diagonals.

Example 2

ABCD is a parallelogram. Its diagonals meet at E, and AE = 6 cm. How long is AC?

The diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other in half, so EC = AE = 6 cm. AC = 6 + 6.

Answer: 12 cm

Line symmetry and rotational symmetry

A line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that match exactly. The order of rotational symmetry is how many times a shape fits onto itself in one full turn. A shape that only fits after a full turn has order 1 (no rotational symmetry).

Congruent shapes

Shapes are congruent when they are exactly the same size and shape. One fits exactly on top of the other after a slide, a turn or a flip. Matching sides are equal and matching angles are equal.

Example 3

Rectangle A is 6 cm by 4 cm. Rectangle B is 8 cm by 3 cm. Are they congruent?

Both have an area of 24 cm², but the sides are different. Congruent shapes need matching sides.

Answer: No

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A square is not a rectangleA rectangle needs only 4 right angles. Every square is a rectangle (and a rhombus)
The diagonals of a rhombus are equalThey cross at right angles, but they are equal only in a square
A rectangle’s diagonals are lines of symmetryFold to check: only the lines through the middles of opposite sides work
A parallelogram has 2 lines of symmetryIt has none, but it has rotational symmetry of order 2
Order 0 for no rotational symmetryEvery shape fits after a full turn, so the smallest order is 1
A flipped or turned shape is not congruentSlides, turns and flips keep size and shape the same
Equal area or equal perimeter means congruentCheck that every side and every angle matches

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about quadrilaterals in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 6 Spatial Sense, students list the properties of quadrilaterals, including their diagonals, line symmetry and rotational symmetry, and they identify and construct congruent shapes.
Yes. A rectangle is any quadrilateral with 4 right angles, and every square has 4 right angles. A square is also a rhombus because its 4 sides are equal.

faq.q: Are the diagonals of a rhombus equal?
faq.a: Not usually. The diagonals of a rhombus cut each other in half at right angles, but they are equal only when the rhombus is a square.

faq.q: What does congruent mean in Grade 6 math?
faq.a: Congruent shapes are exactly the same size and shape, so one fits exactly on the other after a slide, turn or flip. Matching sides and matching angles are equal.

sets.title: Name the quadrilateral from its properties

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides, and each pair is next to each other (not opposite). That makes it a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: A rhombus has one right angle. What is its best name?
items.e: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal and angles next to each other add to 180°. One 90° angle makes all 4 angles 90°, so the rhombus is a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides. Its angles, in order, are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. The angles are not 90°, so it is not a square.

items.q: A rectangle has all 4 sides 12 cm long. What is its best name?
items.e: It has 4 right angles (it is a rectangle) and 4 equal sides. That makes it a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its sides, in order, are 8 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. The sides are not all equal (8 cm and 5 cm), so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle and 4 equal sides make a rhombus. A shape with both is a square, the name that tells the most.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
items.e: Exactly one pair of parallel sides makes a trapezoid. Parallelograms and rhombuses have 2 pairs.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides, and each pair is next to each other (not opposite). That makes it a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: A quadrilateral has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm, in order around the shape. It has no parallel sides. What is its best name?
items.e: The two 5 cm sides are next to each other, and so are the two 9 cm sides. Two pairs of equal sides next to each other make a kite.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is not a rectangle or a rhombus.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right angles, so it is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: A quadrilateral has sides 7 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm and 4 cm (in order) and angles 70°, 110°, 70° and 110°. What is its best name?
items.e: Opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal, so it is a parallelogram. It has no right angles (not a rectangle) and its sides are not all equal (not a rhombus).

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cross at right angles and cut each other in half, but they are not equal. What is it?
items.e: Cutting each other in half at right angles gives a rhombus. The diagonals are not equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral are equal and cut each other in half, but they do not cross at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Diagonals that cut each other in half make a parallelogram. Equal diagonals make it a rectangle. Not at right angles, so not a square.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this kite. Which is true?
c: They do not cross at right angles
Only one is cut in half
They cut each other in half
items.e: The line of symmetry AC cuts the other diagonal BD in half, so BE = ED. But AE is much shorter than EC, so only one diagonal is cut in half.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Its diagonals meet at E. AE = 6 cm. How long is AC?
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram cut each other in half, so E is the middle of AC. AC = 6 + 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rectangle. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length and cut each other in half. They do not cross at right angles unless the rectangle is a square.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Its diagonals meet at E. AC = 14 cm. How long is BD?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so BD = AC = 14 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles and cut each other in half. They are not equal: one is long and one is short.

items.q: ABCD is a kite. Its diagonals meet at E. BD = 10 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: AC is the line of symmetry of the kite, and it cuts BD in half. BE = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this rhombus. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
They do not cross at right angles
They are not equal in length
items.e: The diagonals of this rhombus are different lengths. They do cross at right angles and cut each other in half. Only a square has equal diagonals among rhombuses.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Its diagonals meet at E. BD = 9 cm. How long is AC?
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram are not always equal. Here AC is longer than BD, so knowing BD does not tell you AC.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this kite. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: The diagonals of a kite cross at right angles. The long diagonal cuts the short one in half, but not the other way round.

items.q: ABCD is a square. Its diagonals meet at E. AC = 12 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a square are equal and cut each other in half. BD = 12 cm, so BE = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

items.q: Mei says the diagonals of every rhombus are equal in length. Is she right?
items.e: Equal sides do not mean equal diagonals. A rhombus that is not a square has one long and one short diagonal.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Its diagonals meet at E. What is the size of angle AEB?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles, so angle AEB = 90°. (60° and 120° are angles of the rhombus itself.)

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this parallelogram. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: In every parallelogram the diagonals cut each other in half. In this one they are not equal and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cut each other in half. They are not equal and not at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Diagonals that cut each other in half make a parallelogram. Not equal: not a rectangle. Not at right angles: not a rhombus.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this square. Which is true?
c: Neither one is cut in half
Equal, and cross at right angles
They do not cross at right angles
They are not equal in length
items.e: A square is a rectangle (equal diagonals) and a rhombus (diagonals at right angles). Its diagonals also cut each other in half.

items.q: The diagonals of a quadrilateral cross at right angles, but only one of them is cut in half. What is it?
items.e: In a kite, the line of symmetry cuts the other diagonal in half at a right angle, but is not cut in half itself.

items.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal, cross at right angles and cut each other in half?
items.e: Equal diagonals come from being a rectangle, and right angles where they cross come from being a rhombus. Only a square is both.

items.q: AC and BD are the diagonals of this trapezoid. Which is true?
c: They cut each other in half
items.e: This trapezoid has 2 equal sides (the slanted sides), so its diagonals are equal in length. They do not cut each other in half and do not cross at right angles.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this kite have?
items.e: A kite has 1 line of symmetry, through the corners where the equal sides meet. The other diagonal is not a line of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this parallelogram have?
items.e: This parallelogram has no lines of symmetry. Any fold leaves the slanted corners sticking out. (It does have rotational symmetry.)

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this trapezoid?
c: Yes, the halves match when folded
Only if the shape is turned
Yes, both halves have equal area
No, the halves do not match
items.e: This trapezoid has equal slanted sides, so the line through the middles of the top and bottom is a line of symmetry.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this rhombus?
c: Yes, both halves have equal area
Only if the shape is turned
Yes, the halves match when folded
No, the halves do not match
items.e: Each diagonal of a rhombus is a line of symmetry. Folding on it puts each side exactly on the side next to it.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, through the middles of opposite sides. Its diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this square have?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 2 diagonals and 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides. Turning it does not change this.

items.q: Owen says a rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry because its diagonals are lines of symmetry too. Is he right?
items.e: Folding a rectangle on a diagonal does not make the halves match. Only the 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides work.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this parallelogram?
c: No, the halves do not match
Yes, both halves have equal area
Only if the shape is turned
Yes, the halves match when folded
items.e: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle or a rhombus has no lines of symmetry. Fold it on this line and the slanted sides do not match.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this kite?
c: No, the halves do not match
Yes, both halves have equal area
Yes, the halves match when folded
Only if the shape is turned
items.e: A kite has only 1 line of symmetry, the one through the top and bottom corners. Folding on the cross line puts the short sides on the long sides.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has 4 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 4?
items.e: Only a square has 4 lines of symmetry and fits onto itself after every quarter turn. A rectangle and a rhombus have 2 lines and order 2.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of this parallelogram?
items.e: A parallelogram fits onto itself after a half turn (180°) and after a full turn: order 2. It has rotational symmetry even with no lines of symmetry.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly 2 lines of symmetry, and they are its diagonals. What is it?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus are its lines of symmetry. A rectangle’s lines go through the middles of the sides, and a square has 4 lines.

items.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry of order 2 but no lines of symmetry?
items.e: Shape A is a parallelogram: it fits onto itself after a half turn, but no fold makes the halves match. The rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, and the kite and the trapezoid have 1 line but only order 1.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of this kite?
items.e: A kite only fits onto itself after a full turn, so its order of rotational symmetry is 1 (no rotational symmetry). Order 0 is not used: every shape matches after a full turn.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this rectangle?
c: Only if the shape is turned
Yes, the halves match when folded
No, the halves do not match
Yes, both halves have equal area
items.e: Fold a rectangle along a diagonal and the corners do not land on each other. The two halves have the same area, but equal area is not enough. A rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry, through the middles of opposite sides.

items.q: What is the smallest turn that fits a rectangle (not a square) exactly onto itself?
items.e: After a quarter turn the long sides would stand up, so it does not fit. After a half turn it fits, so the order is 2.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of this square?
items.e: A square fits onto itself after a quarter turn (90°), a half turn, a three-quarter turn and a full turn: 4 times in one full turn, so order 4.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry of this kite?
c: Yes, both halves have equal area
Yes, the halves match when folded
No, the halves do not match
Only if the shape is turned
items.e: The line through the top and bottom corners of a kite is its line of symmetry. Each half is the mirror image of the other.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this trapezoid have?
items.e: This trapezoid has equal slanted sides, so it has 1 line of symmetry, down the middle. The top and bottom are different lengths, so there is no other.

items.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of this rhombus?
items.e: A rhombus fits onto itself after a half turn and a full turn, so the order is 2. A quarter turn does not work unless it is a square.

items.q: Leah traces shape P on tracing paper. How can she check if shape Q is congruent to P?
c: See if the tracing fits on Q
items.e: Congruent shapes fit exactly on top of each other. She may slide, turn or flip the tracing to make it fit.

items.q: Quadrilateral ABCD is congruent to quadrilateral PQRS. A matches P, B matches Q, C matches R and D matches S. The perimeter of ABCD is 26 cm. What is the perimeter of PQRS?
items.e: All 4 matching sides are equal, so the perimeters are equal: 26 cm.

items.q: Are shapes P and Q congruent?
items.e: Q has the same shape as P, but every side is twice as long. Congruent shapes must be the same size too, so they are not congruent.

items.q: Are shapes P and Q congruent?
items.e: Q is P turned a quarter turn. Turning moves a shape but does not change its size or shape, so they are congruent.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape A is the triangle P turned a quarter turn. Its two short sides are still 2 units. The others are larger copies or have a longer side, so they are not the same size.

items.q: Two rectangles both have an area of 24 cm². Are they always congruent?
items.e: 6 cm × 4 cm and 8 cm × 3 cm both have an area of 24 cm², but their sides are different. Same area does not mean congruent.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape D is shape P flipped (a mirror image). A flipped shape is still congruent: same size, same shape. The others have an arm that is shorter, thicker or longer.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape B is shape P turned a quarter turn. Its sides and angles match P exactly. The others are a longer shape, a rectangle and a shape with a shorter top.

items.q: Two rhombuses both have sides of 5 cm. Are they always congruent?
items.e: A rhombus with 5 cm sides can be a square or a thin, slanted shape. Same sides but different angles means not congruent.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape D is the kite P turned a quarter turn. The others have a shorter tail, sides that are all equal, or a wider body.

items.q: Hana wants to draw a rectangle congruent to one that is 6 cm by 4 cm. Which rectangle should she draw?
items.e: A congruent copy has the same side lengths and angles: 6 cm by 4 cm. 12 by 8 is an enlargement, 5 by 5 has the same perimeter and 8 by 3 has the same area, but none of them is the same size and shape.

items.q: Quadrilateral ABCD is congruent to quadrilateral PQRS. A matches P, B matches Q, C matches R and D matches S. Angle B is 115°. What is angle Q?
items.e: Matching angles of congruent shapes are equal. Angle B matches angle Q, so angle Q = 115°.

items.q: Two squares both have sides of 5 cm. Are they congruent?
items.e: Every square with 5 cm sides has the same sides (5 cm) and the same angles (90°), so they are always congruent.

items.q: Kai flips a trapezoid over to make its mirror image. Which is true?
items.e: A reflection keeps every side length and every angle the same, so the image is congruent to the trapezoid.

items.q: Quadrilateral ABCD is congruent to quadrilateral PQRS. A matches P, B matches Q, C matches R and D matches S. CD = 6 cm. Which side of PQRS is also 6 cm?
items.e: C matches R and D matches S, so side CD matches side RS. RS = 6 cm.

items.q: Quadrilateral ABCD is congruent to quadrilateral PQRS. A matches P, B matches Q, C matches R and D matches S. AB = 7 cm. How long is PQ?
items.e: Matching sides of congruent shapes are equal. AB matches PQ, so PQ = 7 cm.

items.q: Are shapes P and Q congruent?
items.e: Q is the mirror image of P. Flipping does not change side lengths or angles, so the shapes are congruent.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape C is shape P turned upside down (a half turn). The others are taller, have a taller roof, or are wider.

items.q: Which move does NOT always give a congruent image?
items.e: Slides, flips and turns move a shape without changing its size or shape. An enlargement changes the size.

items.q: Which shape is congruent to shape P?
items.e: Shape C is shape P turned a quarter turn. The square has the same area as P (4 square units), but equal area does not mean congruent. The other parallelograms have a longer or more slanted side.

items.q: The flag of Canada is a rectangle with a red maple leaf in the middle. How many lines of symmetry does the whole flag have?
items.e: The red–white–red rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, but the maple leaf only matches when folded left to right. Folding top to bottom turns the leaf upside down, so the flag has just 1 line.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: A parallelogram’s diagonals cross at right angles
items.e: The diagonals of every rectangle are equal. A rhombus or a parallelogram has equal diagonals only when it is a rectangle or a square.

items.q: Owen builds a kite for a kite festival in Ottawa. The two wooden sticks are the diagonals of the kite. At what angle do the sticks cross?
items.e: The diagonals of a kite cross at right angles, so the sticks meet at 90°.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
items.e: A rectangle only needs 4 right angles, and every square has them. The other statements are only sometimes true.

items.q: Ava draws a quadrilateral. All 4 sides are 5 cm. Its diagonals are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. The diagonals are different lengths, so it is not a square. (Half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm make 5 cm sides.)

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: Shapes with equal areas are congruent
Shapes with equal perimeters are congruent
A shape and its enlargement are congruent
items.e: Congruent shapes have matching sides of equal length, so their perimeters are equal. The opposite is not true: a 5 × 5 square and a 6 × 4 rectangle have the same perimeter but are not congruent.

items.q: Liam’s dad builds a deck frame. Opposite sides are 4 m and 3 m, so it is a parallelogram. He measures both diagonals: 5 m and 5 m. What does this tell him?
items.e: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle, so all 4 corners are right angles. Builders check corners this way.

items.q: Arjun folds a sheet of letter paper (21.6 cm by 27.9 cm) along a diagonal. Do the two halves match exactly?
items.e: A rectangle that is not a square has no diagonal line of symmetry. The two triangles have equal area, but the corners do not line up.

items.q: Ethan measures a quadrilateral’s diagonals. Both are 10 cm, and they cut each other in half at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Equal diagonals that cut each other in half: rectangle. At right angles too: rhombus. Both: a square.

items.q: Priya sews 8 congruent rhombus patches for a quilt. Each side of one patch is 6 cm. How much ribbon does she need to go around all 8 patches?
items.e: One patch: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. The patches are congruent, so 8 patches need 8 × 24 = 192 cm.

items.q: Benjamin cuts a rectangular piece of cardboard, 30 cm by 20 cm, along one diagonal. What is true about the two pieces?
items.e: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into 2 triangles with sides 30 cm, 20 cm and the diagonal. A half turn puts one exactly on the other, so they are congruent.

items.q: Sofia covers a bulletin board with congruent parallelogram tiles. One tile has sides of 4 cm and 7 cm. What is the perimeter of each tile?
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal: 4 + 7 + 4 + 7 = 22 cm. (28 is 4 × 7, not a perimeter.)

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: A rectangle’s diagonals cross at right angles
A trapezoid’s diagonals cut each other in half
A square’s diagonals cross at right angles
items.e: A square is a rhombus, so its diagonals cross at right angles. The other statements are true only for some of those shapes.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
items.e: A rhombus has 4 equal sides, and its opposite sides are parallel, so it is always a parallelogram.

items.q: Zoe paints a sign shaped like a parallelogram. One angle is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
items.e: Angles next to each other in a parallelogram add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°. The angle opposite the 70° angle is also 70°.

items.q: Which statement is always true?
c: A rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry
A trapezoid has a line of symmetry
A parallelogram fits onto itself after a half turn
A parallelogram has 2 lines of symmetry
items.e: Every parallelogram (including rectangles, rhombuses and squares) matches itself after a half turn. Most parallelograms have no lines of symmetry, and many trapezoids have none.

items.q: Noah’s family builds a garden bed with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are equal. How many lines of symmetry does the garden bed have?
items.e: A trapezoid with equal slanted sides has 1 line of symmetry, through the middles of the 2 parallel sides.

items.q: The short stick of Owen’s kite is 60 cm long, and the long stick crosses it at its middle. How far is the crossing point from each end of the short stick?
items.e: The long diagonal cuts the short one in half: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

items.q: A square cottage window has sides of 80 cm. Two wooden bars run along its diagonals. Each bar is about 113 cm long. About how far from a corner do the bars cross?
items.e: The diagonals of a square cut each other in half: 113 ÷ 2 = 56.5 cm. (40 cm is half a side, not half a diagonal.)

items.q: Mateo makes a stained-glass design from 4 congruent kites placed around a centre point, each one a quarter turn from the next. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the design?
items.e: Each quarter turn moves every kite onto the next one, so the design fits onto itself 4 times in a full turn: order 4.
